parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave a second drink untouched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a number or a moment, but it is the verb of a meeting: to second a motion is to back it.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it formally, which is to support it, both used as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: Like egg one found at the Eisteddfod

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shaped like an egg
second meaning: a member of one of the orders of the Welsh bardic Gorsedd

explanation.surface: Something egg-shaped turns up at a Welsh cultural festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eisteddfod is the Welsh festival of poetry and music, presided over by a Gorsedd of bards, druids and a lesser order whose members carry the same name as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovate is a botanical adjective for egg-shaped, and also the noun for a member of the Welsh bardic order.

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters are put in a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer a young woman into a career in sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailoring is the craft of cutting and sewing clothes to fit, i.e. the making of garments.

wordplay.note: the French word for us, abroad meaning in a foreign language

explanation.surface: Our common sense is on show when we travel overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' often signals a rearrangement, but here it means translating into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British informal speech for practical intelligence and common sense, borrowed from Greek.

parts.note: surface reading: a man who collapses or gives up under trial or pressure
setter's reading: a working dog that pens livestock in a fold during herding competitions

explanation.surface: A man who gives way whenever he is tested.
explanation.walkthrough: To fold is to fail under pressure, but also to drive animals into a pen, and trials are herding contests for working dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie bred to herd livestock competes in such contests, steering the flock into an enclosure.

parts.note: Anna Leonowens, the governess in The King and I
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A Victorian governess has departed, leaving written evidence behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb, but it is the abbreviation for the side. Anna Leonowens taught at the Siamese court, as told in The King and I.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a single year's entry in a chronicle, so it serves as a historical record.

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

parts.note: a ditch is a dug-out trench
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Explorers digging on a field trip strike a source of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' suggests a journey, but here it means speed, as does the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch and expedition both mean promptness and speed in getting something done.

clue.text: Space-traveller encountered Richard on the way up

parts.note: past tense of meet

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Richard Roe, a fictitious name used in English legal cases alongside John Doe

explanation.surface: An astronaut bumped into a man named Richard while climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a lump of rock or dust travelling through space that burns up in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Introduction of poetic licence is commonplace

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word poetic
latitude is freedom of action, a synonym of licence

explanation.surface: A literary critic grumbles that the liberties poets take have become hackneyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite, overused remark, so as a noun it is a synonym for a commonplace.

clue.text: One enters part of church displaying no art

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so the first piece sits within the second

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone walks into a plain church that has no decoration or artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No art' looks like bare church walls, but here art means artfulness or guile.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and unsophisticated, without guile or artfulness, which is what lacking art means here.

clue.text: King gives honour to little boy

parts.note: Order of the British Empire, an honour awarded in the UK
a short form of the boy's name Ronald

explanation.surface: A monarch bestows an award on a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour (Officer of the Order of the British Empire). Oberon is the fairy king in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon rules as monarch of the fairies in Shakespeare's comedy and in English folklore.

definitions.note: names the phrase apple-pie order, of which the answer is the first part
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the phrase for perfect tidiness, from which the adjective comes
second meaning: a baked fruit pudding

explanation.surface: A diner at a restaurant asks for a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a diner's request, but it points to the idiom apple-pie order, meaning perfectly neat. In Britain a sweet is a dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple-pie order is the idiom for perfect neatness, and an apple pie is a common baked dessert.

clue.text: Boarding the ship, one makes a debatable proposition

indicators.note: a passenger boarding a vessel ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the, kept as written, plus SS, the abbreviation for steamship
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A passenger climbs aboard and starts an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition put forward to be argued and defended, as in academic debate.

clue.text: Animal in the paper? That could be the size of it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the large grey mammal with a trunk
second meaning: a traditional large paper size

explanation.surface: A newspaper reader spots a story about a beast and wonders how big it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The size of it' sounds like a comment on how big the creature is, but it is a paper size: elephant folio is a large format for books and drawing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the large mammal, the word names a standard large sheet of drawing or printing paper.

clue.text: Love crumpet that's promiscuous in summer?

indicators.note: promiscuous originally means mixed up indiscriminately, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A saucy holiday-romance headline about a fling during the hot months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but one who does sums. Crumpet is British slang for attractive people regarded sexually, which feeds the racy surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer here is a thing that sums, and a computer is a machine that calculates; the question mark flags the wordplay sense.

parts.note: a part is not the whole
a ridge is a range of hills

explanation.surface: A shooting party finds only some of the birds within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a sport, but it means wild birds shot for food.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a ground bird hunted for sport and food, so it is an example of game.

clue.text: A wise old man, about 100, is up in a tree

definitions.note: describes the answer: someone placed high in a family tree

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the number

parts.note: Nestor, the aged and wise counsellor of the Greeks in the Iliad
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A very old sage of about a hundred has climbed into the branches.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is a family tree, where forebears sit above their descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear appears higher up a genealogical chart than the people descended from them.

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the head, or opening letter, of egg
merging means coming together, a synonym of joining

explanation.surface: An intellectual takes part in the social whirl of young society women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like one word meaning an intellectual, but it splits into egg and head. Debs, short for debutantes, were young upper-class women formally coming out into society.
explanation.definitionFit: Debutantes come out into society, and to come out is to emerge, so this is their characteristic activity.

clue.text: Flag to left of centre of green, significantly

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the following words, just to the left of their midpoint

parts.note: the six letters just before the middle of the eighteen letters

explanation.surface: Golf directions: the pin is placed noticeably left of the middle of the putting surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words run together have eighteen letters; the six ending at the ninth are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag flown by a ship to show its nationality, a naval banner.

parts.note: an orc is a monster of fantasy and folklore
past tense of hide

explanation.surface: A beast lurks hidden among the blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concealed in' looks like a hidden-word signal, but concealed simply supplies its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchid is a large family of exotic flowering plants, so it is an example of a flower.

parts.note: de is French for of
scent is a synonym of perfume

explanation.surface: A dab of perfume from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop of' suggests a small amount of liquid, but Drop alone is the definition, a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a downward slope or fall, the same as a drop in height.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tall glass for sherry or beer
second meaning: a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigging

explanation.surface: A tot of alcohol is poured into a container.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessel suggests a cup or jug to hold the drink, but it is a boat. In Britain a schooner is a large sherry glass; in Australia it is a beer glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a specific glass size for drinks and a two-masted sailing ship.

indicators.note: a wreck is something broken apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small boat at risk of being smashed on the high seas.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the open sea is a place where a small boat could founder.
explanation.definitionFit: The open sea is a vast and dangerous body of water where a small craft could easily come to grief.

clue.text: A scarf gets twisted in a brawl

indicators.note: twisting something out of shape disorders it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's scarf gets pulled out of shape during a punch-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance or quarrel, a close synonym for a fight or scuffle.

parts.note: Chas is the written abbreviation of Charles
east, a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Charles has a serious, solemn demeanour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like an adjective meaning serious, but it is the old verb meaning to carve or engrave.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase metal is to engrave decoration on it, and grave is an archaic verb for the same carving.

parts.note: surface reading: a player lining up in a team made of the best
setter's reading: the combined British and Irish touring side, picked from the best of four nations

explanation.surface: A rugby player takes his place in a team of top talents.
explanation.walkthrough: The British and Irish touring rugby side picks the best players from England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland, and is named after a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Each member of that select touring rugby team takes the animal's name, as the team itself does.

clue.text: Information that is a help to the lamp-holder

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A notice says the following facts will assist whoever carries the light.
explanation.walkthrough: The lamp-holder is Aladdin, whose magic lamp held a spirit that granted wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Aladdin story the spirit from the lamp serves whoever rubs it, so it helps its owner.

clue.text: By no means the best that rider could produce

indicators.note: producing something new from material suggests remaking the letters into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jockey's showing in a race is described as well below par.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means of poor quality, inferior, so it is far from top class.

clue.text: Intended, we hear, to go past in border trespass

indicators.note: going past puts a thing beyond, so this part follows the rest

parts.note: taken as written
a fringe is an edge or border

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken sound, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: meant means intended, and it is said like the common word ending

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately strays across a boundary line onto forbidden ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go past' tells you the sound-alike piece comes after the rest; the ending -ment is said exactly like meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An infringement is a violation or encroachment on rights or property, matching trespass as a noun.
